questions.question: Which one among the following administers the International Development Association (IDA)?
questions.solution: The International Bank of Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association are a part of the World Bank group that began operation in 1944 and was formed to reduce poverty by promoting international trade and capital investment.

questions.question: Who decides the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for agricultural crops in India?

options.text: Commission on Agriculture Cost and Price (CACP)

questions.solution:
• MSP is the minium price at which the government purchases the food grains from the farmers.
 
• CACP was earlier named as Agricultural Prices Commission and came into existence in January 1965.
 
• It’s current chairman is Prof. Vijaya Paul Sharma.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows from south to north?
questions.solution: The Betwa or Betravati is a tributary of the Yamuna. It rises in the Vindhya Range just north of Hoshangabad in Madhya Pradesh and flows north-east through Madhya Pradesh and Orchha to Uttar Pradesh. Other rivers that flow from South to North are Narmada, Chambal, Son and Tugabhadra.

questions.question: Sikhism was founded in which of the following centuries?
questions.solution: Sikhism is based on the spiritual teachings of Guru Nanak, the first Guru and the nine Sikh gurus that succeeded him. The Tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, named the Sikh scripture Guru Granth Sahib as his successor, terminating the line of human Gurus and making the scripture the eternal, religious spiritual guide for Sikhs. It was founded in 15-16th century.

questions.question: For the first time in Gujarat, who implemented Jizya tax?
questions.solution: Jizya is a ktax levied by the Muslim rulers on certain permanent Non-Muslim residents of the Muslim territory under Islamic law. The Umayyad general Muhammad-bin-Qasim, introduced the jizya in India in 712 A.D. when he conquered Sind. It was abolished by Akbar.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest city of Myanmar?
questions.solution: Yangon served as the capital of Myanmar until 2006, when the military government relocated the capital to the purpose-built city of Naypyidaw in central Myanmar. The city is also home to the gilded Shwedagon Pagoda that is Myanmar's most sacred Buddhist pagoda.

questions.question:
Valency of an element depends on which of the following?

I. Number of losing electron

II. Number of gaining electron

III. Number of sharing electron
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

__
 
• Valance Electrons: A valence electron is simply the total number of electrons present in the outermost shell of an atom.
 
• Valency: Valency is the number of** electrons an atom loses, gains or shares**__ with other atoms in order to get a stable configuration.

For example-

Atomic Configuration of Carbon (C ) is ( 6 ) = 2,4

__
 
• The valency of Carbon will be 4 as it needs 4 more electrons to get a stable configuration.
 
• The number of valence electrons in carbon is also four as its outermost shell contains 4 electrons.

Atomic Configuration of Nitrogen N ( 7 ) = 2,5

The valency of nitrogen is 3 as it needs 3 more electrons to complete its octet but the number of valence electrons in nitrogen is 5.

So, 

**It can be losing, gaining or sharing of electrons.**__

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT?

I. Oils containing unsaturated fatty acids should be used for cooking.

II Animal fats have saturated carbon chains.

III. Saturated fatty acids are generally harmful for health
questions.solution: Saturated fats are simply fat molecules that have no double bonds between carbon molecules because they are saturated with hydrogen molecules. Saturated fats are typically solid at room temperature. Some food items that contain saturated fats are fatty beef, pork, lamb etc.

questions.question: In India, who is considered above the law of country?
questions.solution: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees an equality before law and equal protection by law as a fundamental right. This right cannot be breached and the Supreme Court holds the power to issue one of the five writes provided under Article 32 of the Constitution in case of any breach.

questions.question:
Which among the following Article/Articles of Indian Constitution deals with Emergency provisions?

I. Article 352

II. Article 356

III. Article 360
questions.solution:
Article 352

 
 
 
National Emergency, declared when security of India or any part is threatened whether by war or external aggression or an armed rebellion

 
 
 

 
 
Article 356

 
 
 
State Emergency, declared when the Governor feels that State Government is violating the Constitution

 
 
 

 
 
Article 360

 
 
 
Financial Emergency, declared when a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or the credit of India or any part thereof is threatened

questions.question: The transport of soluble products of photosynthesis is called _________.
questions.solution:
• Translocation is the movement of materials from leaves to other tissues throughout the plant.
 
• Plants produce carbohydrates in their leaves by photosynthesis, but non-photosynthetic parts of the plant also require carbohydrates and other organic and nonorganic materials.

questions.question: Which feature of the cell allows or permits the entry and exit of some materials in and out of the cell?
questions.solution:
• The plasma membrane allows or permits the entry and exit of some materials in and out of the cell. 
 
• Some substances like CO₂ or O₂ gases can move across the cell membrane by a process called diffusion.

questions.question: In November 2017, Indian Government launched ‘UMANG’ mobile app. What does ‘G’ stand for in ‘UMANG’?
questions.solution: UMANG or Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance, is a Government of India all-in-one single unified secure multi-channel multi-platform multi-lingual multi-service freeware mobile app for accessing over 1,200 central and state government services in multiple Indian languages services such as AADHAR, Digi Locker etc.

questions.question: What is the name of first solar mission of Indian Space Research Organisation set to be launch in 2019?
questions.solution:
• Aditya (which means Sun) or Aditya-L1 is a spacecraft whose mission is to study the Sun.
 
• It was conceptualised by the Advisory Committee for Space Research in January 2008.
 
• It has been designed and will be built in collaboration between Indian Space Research Organisation and various Indian research organizations and will be launched by ISRO around 2019 or 2020.
 
• This will be the first Indian space mission to study the Sun, and also the first Indian mission to be placed at Lagrangian point L1

questions.question: In October 2017, SEBI directed the stock exchanges to impose how much fine/penalty on those companies which do not comply with the minimum public shareholding norms?
questions.solution: SEBI, in October 2017 announced that non-compliant companies with regard to Minimum Public Shareholding norms will have to pay a fine of ₹5,000 a day. In addition, the entire promoter holding, except for compliance to MPS, will be frozen by depositories, and the promoter group and directors of the particular company will not be allowed to hold any position in other companies.

questions.question: In January 2018, the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017 was notified. Few provisions in the amendment Act have important bearing on the working of the ________.
questions.solution:
• The Amendment Act now allows companies to issue shares at a discount to its creditors when its debt is converted into shares in pursuance of any statutory resolution plan such as resolution plan under the Code or debt restructuring scheme.
 
• The Amendment Act now requires that where a company has defaulted in payment of dues to any bank or public financial institution or non-convertible debenture holders or any other secured creditor, the prior approval of the bank or public financial institution concerned or the non-convertible debenture holders or other secured creditor, as the case may be.

questions.question: Find the potential energy gained by a body of mass 25 kg, if it is raised by 5 m. (use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The gravitational potential energy of an object is the 'stored energy' that the object has by being at that height. This is equivalent to its mass times the force of gravity, ‘g’ times the height of the object. This means following is the formula:

Potential energy = mass × gravity × height.

Potential Energy = 25 × 10 × 5 = 1250 J

questions.question: If the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is g, then the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of a planet whose mass is same as that of earth and radius is twice as that of earth is ___________.
questions.solution:
**__Concept-__**

**Acceleration due to Gravity:**

 
• The force of attraction exerted by the earth on a body is called gravitational pull or gravity. We know that when a force acts on a body, it produces acceleration. Therefore, a body under the effect of gravitational pull must accelerate.

**Acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the earth is –**

g = frac{{GM}}{{{R²}}}

**Explanation – **

As we know that acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the earth is

g = frac{{GM}}{{{R²}}}

Given - M₁ = M and R₁ = 2R

therefore g' = frac{{GM}}{{{{( {2R} )}²}}} = frac{{GM}}{{4{R²}}} = (g)/(4)

questions.question: An _________ is a sudden shaking or trembling of the earth.
questions.solution: An earthquake is the shaking of the surface of the Earth, resulting from the sudden release of energy in the Earth's lithosphere that creates seismic waves. Earthquakes can range in size and are measured in Richter Scale.

questions.question: In Microsoft Word, _______ contains tools for standard tasks like saving, printing, cutting, copying, pasting etc.
questions.solution: The standard toolbar provides a quick shortcut to many frequently used functions. You can customize the buttons that appear on the standard toolbar using the customize toolbar menu item. Standard toolbar functions are file commands, window commands etc.
